Definition: from G4119 and G2192; holding (desiring) more, i.e. eager for gain (avaricious, hence a defrauder):--covetous.
BiblicalUsage: Pleonektes is the covetous man, the one who always wants more. Paul says the covetous shall not inherit the kingdom of God in 1 Corinthians 6:10, and that we are not even to eat with a brother who is covetous in 1 Corinthians 5:11. He is not to be named among saints in Ephesians 5:5, for the covetous man is an idolater.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe covetousness is idolatry with a respectable face — it worships more instead of God. My position is that the cure is contentment, not a bigger barn.
